subject: Whistic onboarding: scope confirmation, KMS evidence & service-account delineation
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmepayments.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@acmepayments.com
Date: 2027-12-19T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Whistic profile kickoff and KMS export

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for agreeing to fast-track our Whistic profile. We completed the initial questionnaire but there are two items the audit team flagged that I'd like to confirm with you before we finalize:

1) KMS key provenance: they want a signed export (or a signed metadata snapshot) that shows the key IDs and rotation schedule for the encryption keys used to encrypt customer data in staging/prod.
2) Service account ownership: we listed a single service account for ingestion, but the reviewer asked for a short role matrix (who can impersonate, who can rotate credentials, who is the steward).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a KMS export (even if redacted) and a small matrix? If so, we can attach in Whistic and mark as final.

Elena
Sr. InfoSec Manager
Acme Payments

Attachments: none
From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmepayments.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-12-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic profile kickoff and KMS export

Elena — thanks for the clear callouts. Short answers up front: yes to both, with a small caveat on the KMS export format.

Details:
- KMS/export: We can provide a metadata export that includes key ARNs/IDs, creation and rotation timestamps, and the KMS policy hash. We avoid sharing raw key material of course; the export will be signed by our key-management team and timestamped.
- Service account matrix: we'll provide a one-page XLS with roles (impersonation, rotation, owner, approver) and names/emails. We'll mark any redacted or shared-managed roles.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll assemble the two artifacts and drop them into a sealed Google Drive folder (link below).
2) Kimberly can provide the signed KMS metadata export; Marissa will own the role matrix and the Whistic attachment 
3) We can then push them into your Whistic profile and leave a short narrative in the evidentiary notes explaining redactions.

Can we target EOD tomorrow (12/20) for the upload?

— Jonas
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmepayments.com>, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-12-20T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Whistic profile kickoff and KMS export — artifacts attached

On Mon, Dec 20, 2027 at 10:18 AM, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com wrote:

Elena / team — attaching the two artifacts we discussed. Notes below.

1) acme-kms-export.txt (signed): contains key IDs, creation_date, last_rotated, rotation_policy_version, and a short policy hash. Redacted fields: key aliases that map directly to customer identifiers have been replaced with stable tokens; full alias mapping available under an NDA if required. The export is PGP-signed by our key-management mailbox.

2) service-account-role-matrix.xlsx: simple sheet with service account name, principal owners, rotation owner, impersonation scope, and a contact email. We added a notes column for accounts that are shared across prod/staging.

We uploaded both to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_kms-evidence (view-only).

If you prefer the files directly in Whistic, Marissa can push them into the evidence tab and update the narrative text.

Thanks — Kim
Staff Security Engineer, Key Management
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-kms-export.txt (text/plain, PGP-signed), service-account-role-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmepayments.com>, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-12-21T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Whistic profile kickoff and KMS export — pushing evidence and short narrative

Elena — I just pushed the two artifacts into your Whistic profile and added a short narrative under the "Encryption & Key Management" and "Service Accounts" evidence fields. Summary of text I added:

- KMS: "Redwood provided a signed metadata export (acme-kms-export.txt) describing key identifiers, rotation cadence, and policy hashes. Sensitive alias values were redacted; Redwood offers a mapping under NDA for higher assurance reviews."
- Service accounts: "A role matrix (service-account-role-matrix.xlsx) documents owners, rotation responsibilities, and impersonation scope for accounts used in ingestion and telemetry pipelines."

I also linked the Drive folder in the Whistic notes and set the evidence status to "Submitted - Under Review." Let me know if you need us to respond in the Q&A or attach a statement signed by our CISO.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
